title: From Slide Design to Smart Code: Automating the 'Do Now' with AI
author: Dario Emanuele
summary: Dario Emanuele announces the completion of his AI lesson-planning ecosystem with a new Do Now Gem that generates fully interactive HTML starter activities. Having previously automated atomisation, lesson planning, HTML slide creation, and worksheet generation, the only remaining manual task was his carefully structured five-question spaced retrieval starter. The new Gem produces a browser-ready HTML file with five questions of escalating challenge (Confidence Builder, Low, Medium, High, and a UKMT competition-standard extension), an embedded drawing canvas for live modelling, click-to-reveal answer buttons, and an auto-populated header, all from a single eight-input prompt. Because the teacher dictates a different topic for each of the five questions, the tool engineers interleaved spaced retrieval rather than blocked practice, while Emanuele frames the whole system as a buffet that preserves teacher agency rather than a mandate.
points: The 'Do Now' was the last manual frontier: with slide-building and worksheets already automated, the new Gem closes the final gap by generating the five-question starter as a browser-ready HTML file.
A five-question escalating architecture (confidence builder, low, medium, high, and UKMT extension) serves all attainment levels within one shared starter, with no separate differentiation needed.
Spaced retrieval is engineered directly into the prompt: each question targets a different topic from the course, forcing interleaving rather than blocked practice.
The generated page includes an embedded drawing canvas and click-to-reveal answer buttons, removing all manual formatting and alignment work for the teacher.
Emanuele frames the tool as a buffet rather than a mandate, preserving professional judgment so teachers adopt AI efficiency without surrendering expertise.
